source_text:
Λέγει δὲ
οὕτως ὁ Παῦλος· Ὁ δὲ βεβαιῶν ἡμᾶς σὺν ὑμῖν εἰς Χριστὸν καὶ χρίσας ἡμᾶς θεός, ὁ καὶ σφραγισάμενος ἡμᾶς καὶ δοὺς τὸν ἀῤῥαβῶνα τοῦ πνεύματος ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν, ὅ ἐστιν, ὅτι ἐβεβαιώθη σὺν ὑμῖν εἰς Χριστόν. Πόθεν τοῦτο ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος, 3 οὗ δέδωκεν ἡμῖν; Ἡ γὰρ ἀπόδειξις, ὧν ἐπηγγείλατο Χριστός, ἐκ τῆς τοῦ πνεύματος παρουσίας ἐστίν· ἐπηγγείλατο βασιλείαν οὐρανῶν, ἐπηγγείλατο ἀφθαρσίαν, ἀθανασίαν, σοφίαν, ἁγιασμόν, ἀπολύτρωσιν. Τίς ταύτης τῆς δωρεᾶς ἀπόδειξις καὶ πόθεν ἡμῖν τὸ ἀσφαλὲς ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος, οὗ ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν; Ὁ γὰρ τὸ αἴτιον τῶν χαρισμάτων δεδωκὼς δώσει καὶ τὰ ἑπόμενα καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἀῤῥαβὼν εἴρηται τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς μελλούσης ἀποκαλύπτεσθαι δόξης. {Μ.} ∆ιὰ τί δὲ καὶ τὰς ἁγίας Μαξίμιλλαν καὶ Πρίσκιλλαν ἀποστρέφεσθε καὶ λέγετε μὴ ἐξὸν εἶναι προφητεύειν γυναιξίν; Οὐκ ἦσαν καὶ τῷ Φιλίππῳ θυγατέρες τέσσαρες προφητεύουσαι καὶ ∆εββῶρα οὐκ ἦν προφῆτις; καὶ ὁ ἀπόστολος οὐ λέγει· Πᾶσα γυνὴ προσευχομένη ἢ προφητεύουσα ἀκατακαλύπτῳ τῇ κεφαλῇ, εἰ οὐκ ἔστιν γυναιξὶν προφητεύειν οὐδὲ προσεύχεσθαι; Εἰ δὲ προσεύχονται, καὶ προφητευέτωσαν. {Ο.} Ἡμεῖς τὰς προφητείας τῶν γυναικῶν οὐκ ἀποστρεφόμεθα, καὶ ἡ ἁγία Μαρία προεφήτευσε λέγουσα· Ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν μακαριοῦσί με πᾶσαι αἱ γενεαί. Καὶ ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς εἶπας ἦσαν τῷ ἁγίῳ Φιλίππῳ θυγατέρες προφητεύουσαι, 457 καὶ Μαρία ἡ ἀδελφὴ Ἀαρὼν προεφήτευεν. Ἀλλ' οὐκ ἐπιτρέπομεν αὐταῖς λαλεῖν ἐν ἐκκλησίαις οὐδὲ αὐθεντεῖν ἀνδρῶν, ὥστε καὶ βίβλους ἐξ ὀνόματος αὐτῶν γράφεσθαι. Τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν ἀκατακαλύπτως αὐτὰς προσεύχεσθαι καὶ προφητεύειν, καὶ οὐ κατῄσχυνε τὴν κεφαλὴν τουτέστιν τὸν ἄνδρα. Μὴ γὰρ οὐκ ἠδύνατο ἡ ἁγία Θεοτόκος Μαρία ἐξ ὀνόματος ἑαυτῆς βιβλία γράψαι; Ἀλλ' οὐκ ἐποίησεν, ἵνα μὴ καταισχύνῃ τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐθεντοῦσα τῶν ἀνδρῶν. {Μ.} Τὸ γὰρ ἀκατακαλύπτῳ τῇ κεφαλῇ προσεύχεσθαι ἢ προφητεύειν ἐστὶ τὸ μὴ γράφειν βιβλία; {Ο.} Καὶ πάνυ. {Μ.} Ἐὰν οὖν λέγῃ ἡ ἁγία Μαρία· Ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν μακαριοῦσίν με πᾶσαι αἱ γενεαί, μετὰ παῤῥησίας λέγει καὶ ἀνακεκαλυμμένως, ἢ οὔ; {Ο.} Ἔχει κάλυμμα τὸν εὐαγγελιστήν. Οὐ γὰρ ἐξ ὀνόματος αὐτῆς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ἀναγέγραπται. {Μ.} Μή μοι τὰς ἀλληγορίας ὡς δόγματα λάμβανε. {Ο.} Μάλιστα μὲν οὖν ὁ ἅγιος Παῦλος καὶ τὰς ἀλληγορίας εἰς τὰς τῶν δογμάτων βεβαιώσεις ἔλαβε λέγων, ὅτι· Ἀβραὰμ δύο γυναῖκας ἔσχεν, ἅτινά εἰσιν ἀλληγορούμενα. Αὗται γάρ εἰσιν αἱ δύο διαθῆκαι. ∆ῶμεν δέ, ὅτι οὐ διὰ ἀλληγορίαν τὸ τῆς κεφαλῆς κάλυμμα. Στῆσόν μοι ἐπὶ πάντων τὴν ἀλληγορίαν, ἐὰν ᾖ πενιχρὰ γυνὴ καὶ μὴ ἔχῃ, τί κατακαλύπτεται, οὐ δεῖ αὐτὴν προσεύχεσθαι οὐδὲ προφητεύειν; {Μ.} Καὶ δύναται εἰς τοσοῦτον εἶναι πενιχρά, ὡς μὴ ἔχειν, τί σκεπάσεται. {Ο.} Πολλάκις μὲν εἴδομεν οὕτως πενιχρὰς γυναῖκας ὥστε μὴ ἔχειν, τί σκεπάσονται. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ αὐτὸς οὐ θέλεις εἶναι πενιχρὰς γυναῖκας ὥστε μὴ ἔχειν, τί σκεπάσονται, τί ποιεῖς ἐπὶ τῶν βαπτιζομένων; Ἆρα οὐ δεῖ αὐτὰς βαπτιζομένας προσεύχεσθαι; Τί δὲ λέγεις καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν ἀνδρῶν τῶν πολλάκις διὰ κάκωσιν σκεπαζομένων τὴν κεφαλήν; Ἆρα καὶ τούτους κωλύεις προσεύχεσθαι ἢ προφητεύειν; {Μ.} Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ, ᾗ προσεύχεται ἢ προφητεύει, ἀνακαλύπτεται. {Ο.} Οὐ δεῖ αὐτὸν ἀδιαλείπτως προσεύχεσθαι, ἀλλὰ παρα 458 κούειν τοῦ ἀποστόλου διδάσκοντος αὐτόν, τοῦ λέγοντος· Ἀδιαλείπτως προσεύχεσθε. Καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα δὲ συμβουλεύεις βαπτιζομένην μὴ προσεύχεσθαι. {Μ.} ∆ιὰ τοῦτο οὖν οὐ δέχεσθε Πρίσκιλλαν καὶ Μαξίμιλλαν, ἐπειδὴ βιβλία συνέταξαν. {Ο.} Οὐ διὰ τοῦτο μόνον, ἀλλ' ὅτι καὶ ψευδοπροφήτιδες γεγόνασι μετὰ τοῦ ἐξάρχου αὐτῶν Μοντανοῦ. {Μ.} Πόθεν, ὅτι ψευδοπροφήτιδες γεγόνασιν; {Ο.} Τὰ αὐτὰ Μοντανῷ εἰρήκασιν; {Μ.} Ναί. {Ο.} Ἠλέγχθη δὲ Μοντανὸς ἐναντία ταῖς θείαις γραφαῖς εἰρηκώς, καὶ αὐταὶ ἄρα αὐτῷ συνεκβληθήσονται. 4
thought_title: The Spirit as down payment and why women may prophesy but not write books
orientation: The Orthodox Christian has just argued that the Holy Spirit is the down payment of promised goods, and now the Montanist turns to the question of women prophesying, citing Priscilla and Maximilla.
pass_a_gloss: And Paul says thus: 'But the one who confirms us with you into Christ and anointed us is God, who also sealed us and gave the down payment of the Spirit in our hearts,' which is, that it was confirmed with you into Christ. From where is this? From the Spirit, which he gave us. For the proof of the things Christ promised is from the presence of the Spirit; he promised the kingdom of heaven, he promised incorruptibility, immortality, wisdom, sanctification, redemption. What is the proof of this gift and from where is the certainty for us? From the Spirit, which he gave us. For the one who has given the cause of the gifts will also give the things that follow, and for this reason the Spirit is called the down payment of the glory that is going to be revealed. {M.} But why do you also reject the holy Maximilla and Priscilla and say that it is not lawful for women to prophesy? Were there not also four daughters prophesying to Philip, and was not Deborah a prophetess? And does not the apostle say: 'Every woman praying or prophesying with uncovered head,' if it is not lawful for women to prophesy or to pray? But if they pray, let them also prophesy. {O.} We do not reject the prophecies of women, and the holy Mary prophesied, saying: 'From now on all generations will call me blessed.' And as you yourself said, there were daughters prophesying to the holy Philip, and Miriam the sister of Aaron prophesied. But we do not permit them to speak in churches nor to have authority over men, so as also to have books written in their own name. For this is to pray and prophesy with uncovered head, and she did not shame the head, that is, the man. For was not the holy Mary the Mother of God able to write books in her own name? But she did not do it, so that she might not shame the head by having authority over men. {M.} For is praying or prophesying with uncovered head the not writing of books? {O.} Yes, very much. {M.} If then the holy Mary says: 'From now on all generations will call me blessed,' does she speak with boldness and unveiled, or not? {O.} She has the evangelist as a covering. For the gospel has not been written down in her name. {M.} Do not take allegories for me as doctrines. {O.} But rather the holy Paul also took allegories for the confirmations of doctrines, saying that: 'Abraham had two wives, which things are allegorized. For these are the two covenants.' But let us grant that the covering of the head is not because of allegory. Set aside for me the allegory in all cases: if a poor woman is and does not have anything to cover herself with, must she not pray nor prophesy? {M.} And can she be so poor as not to have anything to cover herself with? {O.} We have often seen women so poor that they do not have anything to cover themselves with. But since you yourself do not want there to be poor women so as not to have anything to cover themselves with, what do you do in the case of those being baptized? Must they not pray while being baptized? And what do you say also in the case of men who often because of affliction cover their head? Do you also forbid these to pray or prophesy? {M.} In that hour in which he prays or prophesies, he uncovers. {O.} He must not pray without ceasing, but disobey the apostle who teaches him, who says: 'Pray without ceasing.' And you advise the woman being baptized not to pray. {M.} For this reason therefore you do not accept Priscilla and Maximilla, because they composed books. {O.} Not for this reason only, but because they also have been false prophetesses along with their leader Montanus. {M.} From where, that they have been false prophetesses? {O.} Did they say the same things as Montanus? {M.} Yes. {O.} But Montanus was convicted of having spoken contrary to the divine Scriptures, and they therefore will also be cast out with him.

choices.why: The glossary fixes ἀῤῥαβών as 'down payment'; the genitive is possessive, the Spirit is the down payment.
The glossary fixes this phrase as 'with uncovered head'; the dative is instrumental.
The verb means to exercise authority; the genitive marks the object over whom authority is exercised.
The glossary fixes ψευδοπροφήτης as 'false prophet'; the feminine plural form is rendered accordingly.
The glossary fixes ἀλληγορία as 'allegory'; the plural is rendered naturally.
The term means the one who leads or begins; 'leader' fits the context of Montanus as the head of the movement.

pass_b_english: Paul says it this way: 'Now it is God who establishes us with you in Christ and has anointed us, who also sealed us and gave us the down payment of the Spirit in our hearts' (2 Corinthians 1:21-22). That is, we have been established with you in Christ. How do we know this? From the Spirit he has given us. For the proof of what Christ promised comes from the presence of the Spirit. He promised the kingdom of heaven; he promised incorruptibility, immortality, wisdom, sanctification, redemption. What is the proof of this gift, and where does our certainty come from? From the Spirit he has given us. For the one who has given the cause of the gifts will also give what follows from them, and for this reason the Spirit is called the down payment of the glory that is going to be revealed.

The Montanist said: 'Why do you reject the holy Maximilla and Priscilla and say that women are not permitted to prophesy? Did not Philip have four daughters who prophesied, and was not Deborah a prophetess? And does not the apostle say, "Every woman who prays or prophesies with uncovered head" (1 Corinthians 11:5)? If it is not permitted for women to prophesy, neither to pray? But if they pray, let them also prophesy.'

The Orthodox Christian said: 'We do not reject the prophecies of women. The holy Mary also prophesied, saying, "From now on all generations will call me blessed" (Luke 1:48). And as you yourself said, the holy Philip had daughters who prophesied, and Miriam the sister of Aaron prophesied. But we do not permit them to speak in the churches or to have authority over men, so as to write books in their own name. For this is to pray and prophesy with uncovered head, and so that she would not shame her head, that is, the man. Could not the holy Mary the Mother of God have written books in her own name? But she did not do so, so that she would not shame her head by having authority over men.'

The Montanist said: 'So praying or prophesying with uncovered head means not writing books?' The Orthodox Christian said: 'Exactly.' The Montanist said: 'If then the holy Mary says, "From now on all generations will call me blessed," does she speak with boldness and with uncovered head, or not?' The Orthodox Christian said: 'She has a covering: the evangelist. For the gospel is not written in her name.'

The Montanist said: 'Do not take allegories as doctrines for me.' The Orthodox Christian said: 'Above all, the holy Paul took allegories for the confirmation of doctrines, saying: "Abraham had two wives, which are spoken allegorically. For these are the two covenants" (Galatians 4:22, 24). But let us grant that the covering of the head is not because of allegory. Apply the allegory in all cases for me: if a woman is poor and does not have anything to cover herself with, should she not pray or prophesy?' The Montanist said: 'Can a woman be so poor that she has nothing to cover herself with?' The Orthodox Christian said: 'We have often seen women so poor that they had nothing to cover themselves with. But since you do not want there to be women so poor that they have nothing to cover themselves with, what do you do in the case of those being baptized? Should they not pray when they are baptized? And what do you say about men who often cover their heads because of hardship? Do you also forbid them to pray or prophesy?' The Montanist said: 'At that hour when she prays or prophesies, she uncovers herself.' The Orthodox Christian said: 'Is he not to pray without ceasing, but to disobey the apostle who teaches him, saying, "Pray without ceasing" (1 Thessalonians 5:17)? And do you advise a woman being baptized not to pray?'

The Montanist said: 'So this is why you do not accept Priscilla and Maximilla: because they composed books.' The Orthodox Christian said: 'Not only for this reason, but also because they were false prophetesses along with their leader Montanus.' The Montanist said: 'How do you know they were false prophetesses?' The Orthodox Christian said: 'Did they say the same things as Montanus?' The Montanist said: 'Yes.' The Orthodox Christian said: 'Montanus was convicted of speaking contrary to the divine Scriptures, and therefore they too will be cast out with him.'

problems.quote: For this is what it means for them to pray and prophesy with uncovered head, and it shames the head
problems.source_quote: Τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν ἀκατακαλύπτως αὐτὰς προσεύχεσθαι καὶ προφητεύειν, καὶ οὐ κατῄσχυνε τὴν κεφαλὴν
problems.why: The Greek says καὶ οὐ κατῄσχυνε (aorist, 'and she did not shame'), but English has present 'it shames'. More critically, the subject changes: the source says Mary (or the woman who covers) 'did not shame her head', but English makes 'it' (the act of uncovering) shame the head. Also 'οὐ' = 'not' is omitted in sense—English says 'it shames' where source says 'she did not shame'.
problems.fix: For this is to pray and prophesy with uncovered head, and she did not shame her head

problems.quote: Should he not pray without ceasing
problems.why: Source is statement: 'He must/ought to pray without ceasing' (οὐ δεῖ = 'it is necessary'). English turns it into a question with 'Should he not', which with the following 'but rather disobey' creates a rhetorical question expecting 'no'. But actually the structure is tricky: 'Must he not pray... but rather disobey?' This is rhetorical, but the Greek οὐ δεῖ is stronger—'he must pray'. The English question form weakens the command.
problems.fix: He must pray without ceasing

problems.quote: At that hour when he prays or prophesies, he uncovers his head.
problems.source_quote: Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ, ᾗ προσεύχεται ἢ προφητεύει, ἀνακαλύπτεται.
problems.why: Source says 'she uncovers herself' (woman); English uses 'he' and 'his head', wrong gender.
problems.fix: At that hour when she prays or prophesies, she uncovers herself.
problems.ruling: ἀνακαλύπτεται is passive/deponent; context is woman (γυναῖκα) just discussed; 'he' misleads.

problems.quote: it shames the head
problems.why: Source has οὐ (not) + κατῄσχυνε (shamed): 'and she did not shame her head'. English drops the negation, flipping the meaning from 'she did not shame' to 'it shames'.
problems.fix: and she did not shame her head
problems.ruling: Source 'καὶ οὐ κατῄσχυνε' = 'and she did not shame'; English 'it shames' drops οὐ, reversing meaning.

problems.quote: Set aside allegory for me in all cases
problems.source_quote: Στῆσόν μοι ἐπὶ πάντων τὴν ἀλληγορίαν
problems.why: στῆσον means 'set up/establish' or here 'put to the test/apply'. 'Set aside' means the opposite—'remove from consideration'. The Orthodox speaker is saying 'apply/test the allegory in all cases', not 'set it aside'.
problems.fix: Apply the allegory in all cases for me
problems.ruling: Στῆσον means 'set up/apply'; 'set aside' means remove, opposite of speaker's intent to apply allegory everywhere.

edits.old: For this is what it means for them to pray and prophesy with uncovered head, and it shames the head
edits.new: For this is to pray and prophesy with uncovered head, and she did not shame her head

edits.old: Should he not pray without ceasing
At that hour when he prays or prophesies, he uncovers his head.
edits.new: At that hour when she prays or prophesies, she uncovers herself.

edits.old: Set aside allegory for me in all cases
edits.new: Apply the allegory in all cases for me

fixed: The negation problem is fixed by the first edit, which restores 'she did not shame her head'.
The gender problem is fixed by the third edit, which restores the feminine subject.

problems.quote: He must pray without ceasing, but rather disobey the apostle who teaches him
problems.source_quote: Οὐ δεῖ αὐτὸν ἀδιαλείπτως προσεύχεσθαι, ἀλλὰ παρακούειν τοῦ ἀποστόλου διδάσκοντος αὐτόν
problems.why: English 'He must pray without ceasing, but rather disobey' misrepresents the Greek. Οὐ δεῖ means 'He must not' or 'It is not right for him'; the Orthodox speaker is saying the Montanist's position leads to absurdity: 'Must he not pray without ceasing, but rather disobey...?' English 'He must pray' flips to an affirmative command, losing the ironic/reductio force. The Greek is sarcastic: 'So he shouldn't pray without ceasing, but rather disobey...?' or 'Is he not to pray without ceasing, but to disobey...?'
problems.fix: So he is not to pray without ceasing, but to disobey the apostle who teaches him?

problems.quote: He must pray without ceasing, but rather disobey
problems.source_quote: Οὐ δεῖ αὐτὸν ἀδιαλείπτως προσεύχεσθαι, ἀλλὰ παρακούειν τοῦ ἀποστόλου
problems.why: Same as mistranslation above: οὐ δεῖ is 'it is not right/necessary' or 'he must not', not 'he must'. The rhetorical question expects 'no' as answer. English affirmative 'He must pray' destroys the reductio ad absurdum.
problems.fix: So he is not to pray without ceasing, but to disobey the apostle?
problems.ruling: Οὐ δεῖ αὐτὸν ἀδιαλείπτως προσεύχεσθαι means 'he must not pray without ceasing'; English 'He must pray' reverses meaning, destroying the argument.

edits.old: He must pray without ceasing, but rather disobey the apostle who teaches him
edits.new: So he is not to pray without ceasing, but to disobey the apostle who teaches him

fixed: The two reported problems are the same issue: the Greek Οὐ δεῖ means 'he must not' or 'it is not right for him', not 'he must'. The English affirmative 'He must pray' flips the meaning and loses the reductio ad absurdum. Changed to 'So he is not to pray without ceasing, but to disobey the apostle who teaches him'.

problems.quote: and she did not shame her head, that is, the man
problems.source_quote: καὶ οὐ κατῄσχυνε τὴν κεφαλὴν τουτέστιν τὸν ἄνδρα
problems.why: The source uses the negative 'ou' (not), but the English omits it, reversing the theological point that the woman did not shame her head.
problems.fix: and she did not shame her head, that is, the man

problems.quote: So he is not to pray without ceasing, but to disobey the apostle
problems.source_quote: Οὐ δεῖ αὐτὸν ἀδιαλείπτως προσεύχεσθαι, ἀλλὰ παρακούειν τοῦ ἀποστόλου
problems.why: The source states he is not to pray without ceasing (a negative command), but the English renders it as a positive command to disobey, altering the logical flow.
problems.fix: He is not to pray without ceasing, but to disobey the apostle

problems.quote: If it is not permitted for women to prophesy, neither is it permitted for them to pray.
problems.source_quote: εἰ οὐκ ἔστιν γυναιξὶν προφητεύειν οὐδὲ προσεύχεσθαι;
problems.why: Source says 'if it is not [permitted] for women to prophesy nor to pray?' — a question, not a statement. English turns rhetorical question into assertion.
problems.fix: If it is not permitted for women to prophesy, neither to pray?
problems.ruling: Source has question mark; English turns rhetorical question into flat assertion, misleading.

problems.quote: On the contrary, the holy Paul took allegories for the confirmation of doctrines
problems.source_quote: Μάλιστα μὲν οὖν ὁ ἅγιος Παῦλος καὶ τὰς ἀλληγορίας εἰς τὰς τῶν δογμάτων βεβαιώσεις ἔλαβε
problems.why: Source says 'especially/most of all' (μάλιστα), not 'on the contrary' (which would be ἀλλά or τοὐναντίον).
problems.fix: Most of all, the holy Paul took allegories for the confirmation of doctrines
problems.ruling: Μάλιστα μὲν οὖν means 'especially/most of all indeed,' not 'on the contrary'; wrong adversative force.

problems.quote: And you advise a woman being baptized not to pray.
problems.source_quote: Καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα δὲ συμβουλεύεις βαπτιζομένην μὴ προσεύχεσθαι.
problems.why: This is also a question in context: 'And do you advise a woman being baptized not to pray?' English states it as fact.
problems.fix: And do you advise a woman being baptized not to pray?
problems.ruling: Context shows continuing rhetorical question; English period makes false statement of fact.

edits.old: For this is to pray and prophesy with uncovered head, and she did not shame her head, that is, the man.
edits.new: For this is to pray and prophesy with uncovered head, and she did not shame her head, that is, the man.

edits.old: So he is not to pray without ceasing, but to disobey the apostle who teaches him, saying, "Pray without ceasing" (1 Thessalonians 5:17)?
edits.new: He is not to pray without ceasing, but to disobey the apostle who teaches him, saying, "Pray without ceasing" (1 Thessalonians 5:17)?

edits.old: If it is not permitted for women to prophesy, neither is it permitted for them to pray.
edits.new: If it is not permitted for women to prophesy, neither to pray?

edits.old: On the contrary, the holy Paul took allegories for the confirmation of doctrines
edits.new: Most of all, the holy Paul took allegories for the confirmation of doctrines

edits.old: And you advise a woman being baptized not to pray.
edits.new: And do you advise a woman being baptized not to pray?

fixed: The first problem was already correct in the English: 'and she did not shame her head, that is, the man' matches the source.
The second problem was fixed by removing 'So' to make it a negative command rather than a positive command.
The third problem was fixed by changing the statement into a question.
The fourth problem was fixed by changing 'On the contrary' to 'Most of all'.
The fifth problem was fixed by changing the statement into a question.

problems.quote: the perfect of the Holy Spirit—that is, the Advocate
problems.why: Intro uses 'Paraclete' but dialogue uses only 'Advocate' for same Greek term.
problems.fix: Use 'Paraclete/Advocate' consistently or note equivalence.

problems.quote: Paul says it this way: 'Now it is God who establishes us with you in Christ and has anointed us, who also sealed us and gave us the down payment of the Spirit in our hearts' (2 Corinthians 1:21-22).

Speaker problem: The source begins with 'Λέγει δὲ οὕτως ὁ Παῦλος' ('And Paul says thus'), which is a continuation of the Orthodox speaker's argument from the previous section; no speaker label is required in the English.

Do you also forbid these to pray or prophesy?'), and the Orthodox speaker then turns to baptism as a parallel case; the English follows the source order correctly.
Mistranslation problem: The Greek 'ἵνα μὴ καταισχύνῃ τὴν κεφαλὴν' is a purpose clause ('so that she would not shame the head'), so the English has been corrected to reflect purpose.
